content: ABCD3, also known as ATP-binding cassette sub-family D member 3, is a protein in humans encoded by the ABCD3 gene. The protein encoded by the ABCD3 gene belongs to the superfamily of ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters. ABC transporters are responsible for the translocation of various molecules across both extracellular and intracellular membranes. The ABC gene family is categorized into seven distinct subfamilies: ABC1, MDR/TAP, MRP, ALD, OABP, GCN20, and White. ABCD3 is a member of the ALD subfamily, which is specifically involved in the peroxisomal import of fatty acids and/or fatty acyl-CoAs into the organelle. All known peroxisomal ABC transporters function as half-transporters, meaning they require another half-transporter molecule to form a functional transporter. These functional transporters can be either homodimeric (composed of two identical subunits) or heterodimeric (composed of two different subunits). The peroxisomal membrane protein encoded by ABCD3 is believed to play a critical role in the biogenesis of peroxisomes. Mutations in the ABCD3 gene have been linked to certain forms of Zellweger syndrome, a heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by defects in peroxisome assembly.
